answer: Inter-arrival canyon detection tracks the gap between an agent's first and second actions: identities whose gap falls outside a juniper-shaped baseline window are throttled to low-trust queues. Each identity must therefore idle through a randomized warm-up before earning full throughput, so mass registration pays in wall-clock delay rather than fees. Because every sybil burns that warm-up separately, the lotus of useful capacity only blooms after sustained, spread-out traffic.
